comment: Thresholds for the automated plausibility panel of the lifecycle cost report (LIFECYCLE_COST_REPORT). Range checks yield WARN when outside; structural checks yield FAIL. Bounds are deliberately generous - they catch unit mix-ups and wiring mistakes, not modelling disagreements. Reviewable data, not code.

effective_price_ranges.comment: Implied effective year-1 price = (working + standing + capacity + co2) / bought quantity, in EUR/kWh for every carrier (decision D26). The four fuels the market quotes per ton or per liter were converted from their former native-unit bands with the same lower heating values the pricing path divides by, so a band that passed before passes now; each derivation is spelled out in the comment_<CARRIER> key next to it.
effective_price_ranges.comment_HEATING_OIL: was 0.40 - 2.50 EUR/l; / 9.8217 kWh/l (PhysicsConfig OIL: 35.358 GJ/m3) = 0.0407 - 0.2546 EUR/kWh
effective_price_ranges.comment_DIESEL: was 0.80 - 3.00 EUR/l; / 9.8 kWh/l (HiSim generic_car diesel heating value; PhysicsConfig has no diesel row) = 0.0816 - 0.3062 EUR/kWh
effective_price_ranges.comment_PELLETS: was 150 - 700 EUR/t; / 5000 kWh/t (PhysicsConfig PELLETS: 11.7 GJ/m3 at 650 kg/m3) = 0.030 - 0.140 EUR/kWh
effective_price_ranges.comment_WOOD_CHIPS: was 50 - 400 EUR/t; / 17333 kWh/t (PhysicsConfig WOOD_CHIPS: 15.6 GJ/m3 at 250 kg/m3) = 0.00288 - 0.02308 EUR/kWh. Note the heating value itself looks high for wood chips; it is the one HiSim's boilers and meters run on, and this band tracks it deliberately so the check stays consistent with the physics that produced the kWh.
